description: FortiGate health, interfaces, VPN, SD-WAN, switching, WiFi and routing via fortigate_exporter

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Average CPU usage across all cores.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: System memory usage. FortiOS enters conserve mode at high memory usage.

panels.title: Sessions
panels.description: Current sessions, all protocols.

panels.title: CPU temp
panels.description: Hottest CPU temperature sensor. No data on VMs.

panels.title: Exporter
panels.description: Whether the last probe of this firewall by fortigate_exporter succeeded.

panels.title: WAN links down
panels.description: SD-WAN members and link-monitor targets whose state is currently down.

targets.expr: (count(max by (interface) (fortigate_virtual_wan_status{instance=~"$firewall",state="down"}) == 1) or vector(0)) + (count(max by (link) (fortigate_link_status{instance=~"$firewall",state="down"}) == 1) or vector(0))

panels.title: IPsec down
panels.description: Site-to-site IPsec phase 2 selectors that are down. Dial-up tunnels (see the 'Dial-up tunnels' variable) are excluded, since they are down whenever no client is connected.

panels.title: Certs expiring
panels.description: Certificates referenced in the configuration that expire within 30 days or have already expired. Details in the Certificates row.

targets.expr: count(((fortigate_certificate_valid_to_seconds{instance=~"$firewall"} - time()) < 30 * 86400) and on (instance, name, scope, vdom, source) (fortigate_certificate_cmdb_references{instance=~"$firewall"} > 0)) or vector(0)

panels.title: FortiOS version
panels.description: Firmware version of the active (primary) node.

targets.expr: (fortigate_version_info{instance=~"$firewall"} and on (instance, serial) (fortigate_ha_member_has_role{instance=~"$firewall",role="root_master"} == 1)) or (fortigate_version_info{instance=~"$firewall"} unless on (instance) fortigate_ha_member_has_role{instance=~"$firewall",role="root_master"})

panels.title: Active node
panels.description: Hostname of the HA primary. 'Standalone' when the firewall is not in an HA cluster.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since the last reboot.

panels.title: Clock drift
panels.description: Difference between the firewall clock and the Prometheus scrape time. Includes probe latency, so a few seconds is normal; large values point to NTP problems.

panels.title: FortiAnalyzer
panels.description: Whether the FortiAnalyzer log queue is connected.

panels.title: FortiManager
panels.description: FortiManager management tunnel state.

panels.title: VPN clients
panels.description: Connected dial-up (remote access) IPsec clients.

panels.title: CPU per core
panels.description: CPU usage per processor core.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: System memory usage. Dashed line marks the conserve-mode danger zone.

panels.title: Sessions
panels.description: Current sessions by protocol (stacked).

panels.title: VDOM resources
panels.description: CPU and memory usage per VDOM (needs the System/VDOMResources probe).

panels.title: HA members
panels.description: Per-member load in the HA cluster. If the members' session counts differ a lot, session sync is likely broken. Net usage is the raw net_usage value FortiOS reports.

panels.title: VDOM licenses
panels.description: VDOMs in use versus the licensed maximum.

panels.title: Temperatures
panels.description: All temperature sensors.

panels.title: Fans
panels.description: Fan speeds. A fan at 0 RPM is shown in red.

panels.title: Voltages
panels.description: Power rail voltages.

panels.title: Sensor alarms
panels.description: Sensors FortiOS itself flags as outside their thresholds.

panels.title: Power supplies
panels.description: PSU status per power supply.

panels.title: Top interfaces by throughput
panels.description: The 10 busiest interfaces. Receive is plotted up, transmit down.

panels.title: Link utilization
panels.description: Current throughput as a share of the negotiated link speed (top 10 per direction).

panels.title: Interface status
panels.description: Link state and negotiated speed. Filter with the column header funnel.

panels.title: Top interfaces by packet rate
panels.description: Packets per second, top 10 per direction.

panels.title: Interface errors
panels.description: Only interfaces with errors are shown. Errors usually mean a bad cable, SFP or duplex mismatch.

panels.title: $interface
panels.description: Throughput of a single interface.

panels.title: Dial-up VPN clients
panels.description: Connected remote-access IPsec clients over time.

panels.title: SSL VPN
panels.description: SSL VPN users and tunnels (no data if SSL VPN is not used).

panels.title: Site-to-site tunnels
panels.description: Site-to-site phase 2 selectors that are up and down (dial-up excluded).

panels.title: IPsec tunnel history
panels.description: Up/down history per site-to-site phase 2 selector. Red bars show outages.
Current state per phase 2 selector, down first.
panels.title: IPsec status
Connected Firewall Users
panels.description: Authenticated firewall users (FSSO, RADIUS, VPN) seen in the selected time range. Rows highlighted green are connected now.

panels.title: Top IPsec tunnels by throughput
panels.description: The 10 busiest phase 2 selectors. Receive up, transmit down.

panels.title: $phase2
panels.description: Throughput of a single phase 2 selector.

panels.title: SD-WAN member state
panels.description: Health-check state per member and SLA. Disabled members also show as down.

panels.title: Latency
panels.description: Health-check round-trip latency.

panels.title: Jitter
panels.description: Health-check jitter.

panels.title: Packet loss
panels.description: Health-check packet loss.

panels.title: Member bandwidth
panels.description: Traffic per SD-WAN member. Receive up, transmit down.

panels.title: Member sessions
panels.description: Active sessions per SD-WAN member.

panels.title: Last state change
panels.description: When each member last changed health-check state.

panels.title: Health-check probes
panels.description: Health-check probe packets per second sent and received. Sent without received means the target is unreachable.

panels.title: Link monitors
panels.description: Link-monitor targets (config system link-monitor).

panels.title: Top policies by active sessions
panels.description: Policies with the most active sessions right now.

panels.title: Top policies by hit rate
panels.description: New sessions matched per second.

panels.title: Top policies by bandwidth
panels.description: Traffic per policy.

panels.title: Top policies by packet rate
panels.description: Packets per second per policy.

panels.title: Policies with zero hits
panels.description: Candidates for cleanup. Hit counters reset on reboot and when a policy is changed, so check Uptime before deleting anything.

panels.title: Switches
panels.description: Managed FortiSwitches.

panels.title: PoE used
panels.description: Total PoE power drawn.

panels.title: PoE budget
panels.description: Total PoE budget of the selected switches.

panels.title: PoE usage
panels.description: PoE power drawn as a share of the budget.

panels.title: Port errors
panels.description: Ports with errors in the selected time range. CRC errors usually mean a bad cable.

targets.expr: (sum by (switch_name, port) (increase(fortigate_managed_switch_rx_errors_total{instance=~"$firewall", switch_name=~"$fortiswitch"}[$__range])) + sum by (switch_name, port) (increase(fortigate_managed_switch_tx_errors_total{instance=~"$firewall", switch_name=~"$fortiswitch"}[$__range]))) > 0

(sum by (switch_name, port) (increase(fortigate_managed_switch_rx_drops_total{instance=~"$firewall", switch_name=~"$fortiswitch"}[$__range])) + sum by (switch_name, port) (increase(fortigate_managed_switch_tx_drops_total{instance=~"$firewall", switch_name=~"$fortiswitch"}[$__range]))) > 0

panels.title: Top switch ports by throughput
panels.description: The 10 busiest switch ports. Receive up, transmit down.

panels.title: Access points
panels.description: Managed APs by status.

panels.title: Wireless clients
panels.description: Connected WiFi clients.
Connected clients per AP.
panels.title: Clients per AP
Channel utilization
panels.description: Airtime used on each radio's channel. Above ~60% clients will notice slowness.

panels.title: Radio TX retries
panels.description: Share of frames that needed retransmission. High values mean interference or weak signal.

panels.title: Interfering APs
panels.description: Foreign APs heard on the same channel, per radio.

panels.title: AP CPU
panels.description: CPU usage per AP.

panels.title: AP memory
panels.description: Memory used per AP.

panels.title: AP inventory
panels.description: Managed APs, their profile and firmware.

panels.title: Selected client
panels.description: Pick a client with the 'WiFi client' variable.

panels.title: Client retries / discards
panels.description: Retransmitted and discarded frames for the selected client.

panels.title: BGP neighbors
panels.description: BGP peers and the number of prefixes received / selected as best path.

panels.title: BGP session history
panels.description: BGP state per neighbor. Anything other than green means the session is down.

panels.title: OSPF neighbors
panels.description: OSPF adjacencies. A healthy adjacency is Full.

panels.title: IP pool usage
panels.description: Share of each NAT IP pool in use. A full pool means new sessions cannot be NATed.

panels.title: FortiAnalyzer registration
panels.description: Registration and connection state reported by FortiOS.

panels.title: FortiAnalyzer queue
panels.description: Whether the log queue to FortiAnalyzer is connected.

panels.title: FortiManager
panels.description: FortiManager connection and registration state.

panels.title: SDN connectors
panels.description: Fabric/SDN connectors and when they last synced.

panels.title: Log disk
panels.description: Local log disk usage.

panels.title: Exporter probe duration
panels.description: How long fortigate_exporter takes to probe this firewall. The red line is the 10 s Prometheus scrape_timeout; probes slower than that fail.

panels.title: Exporter probe success
panels.description: Gaps or red bars mean the exporter could not collect data.

panels.title: Certificates
panels.description: All certificates, soonest expiry first. 'Used by' is how many configuration objects reference the certificate; expired certificates that nothing uses can be ignored.

targets.expr: (fortigate_certificate_valid_to_seconds{instance=~"$firewall"} - time()) / 86400 * on (instance, name, scope, vdom, source) group_left(status, type) fortigate_certificate_info{instance=~"$firewall"}
fortigate_certificate_valid_to_seconds{instance=~"$firewall"} * 1000 * on (instance, name, scope, vdom, source) group_left(status, type) fortigate_certificate_info{instance=~"$firewall"}
fortigate_certificate_cmdb_references{instance=~"$firewall"} * on (instance, name, scope, vdom, source) group_left(status, type) fortigate_certificate_info{instance=~"$firewall"}

list.name: vpn_clients
list.label: Dial-up tunnels (regex)
list.description: Regex matching dial-up/remote-access phase 1 names, e.g. (dialup|remote-vpn).*  Used to count VPN clients and to exclude dial-up tunnels from site-to-site status. Leave empty if you have no dial-up VPN.

title: FortiNET
